subject: Private deployment observability: onboarding evidence & export access patterns
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@globex.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: security@globex.com
Date: 2026-09-15 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: onboarding evidence & export access patterns

Diego —

Thanks for the quick demo this morning. Our security team needs a concise manifest of what observability artefacts Redwood can export from a VPC/on‑prem private instance and the supported transfer patterns (push vs pull, presigned uploads, mutual TLS, etc.). Specifically: 

- Which logs/metrics/traces are available by default from the Private package (system + agent + inference runtime)?
- Supported export endpoints (Splunk HEC, S3 presigned, HTTPS POST to our collector) and recommended auth modes.
- Network egress requirements (CIDR/IP ranges, ports) and recommendations for secure handoff during audits.
- If you support certificate rotation for mTLS endpoints and how we validate evidence for SOC audits.

We'd like a short runbook we can hand to our infra team. Can you include a sample minimal firewall allowlist and an evidence bundle example we can attach to our internal audit ticket?

Alex
Director, Cloud Security — Globex Corp

--
Note: we will need an SLA for evidence retention if retention differs from hosted offerings.

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@globex.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-15 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: onboarding evidence & export access patterns

Alex —

Appreciate the specificity. I put together a short checklist and attached a "manifest" PDF and a small CSV of network requirements (attached). High level:

1) Artefacts included out of the box (Private bundle):
   - System logs (collector, agent, kubelet/systemd where applicable)
   - Inference runtime logs (request/response summaries, model-worker health)
   - Metrics via Prometheus exporter (CPU/GPU, queue latencies, per-route token rates)
   - Tracing hooks (OpenTelemetry spans emitted by runtime with X-Trace-Id support)

2) Supported export patterns:
   - Push to Splunk HEC (mTLS preferred; token-based fallback). We recommend mTLS for on‑prem intake.
   - Push to S3 using presigned PUT URLs for batched evidence bundles (used for audit transfer).
   - HTTPS POST to customer collector with Bearer token or mutual TLS.
   - Optional SFTP drop for air‑gapped customers via a trusted transfer node (customer-provided).

3) Network egress recommendations (see attached CSV):
   - Minimal ports: 443 outbound for HTTPS; 8088/8089 for Splunk HEC depending on config.
   - Allowlist by FQDN + static egress IPs when using Redwood-managed forwarder. If the customer hosts the collector, allow only the collector IPs.
   - For presigned uploads we only need outbound HTTPS to your S3 endpoint.

4) mTLS and certificate rotation:
   - We support mutual TLS for Splunk and HTTPS endpoints. Redwood will ship a CA-signed server cert for managed forwarders; customers can provide their own certs for strict pinning.
   - Certificate rotation can be automated via ACME on supported platforms or via a rotation job that rotates client certs and publishes CSR results to a signed artifact. Audit timestamps and rotation events are logged into the evidence bundle.

5) Evidence bundle example and retention:
   - Bundle contains manifest.json (hashes & timestamps), sample logs (redacted), and a trace-sample (OTLP). We include signing metadata (who exported, SHA256 checksums).
   - Retention is configurable on Private installs; default is 90 days for on‑prem packages unless negotiated.

Attachments: redwood_private_evidence_manifest_v1.pdf, splunk_hec_network_requirements.csv

I'll loop in Kimberly to finalize the runbook and produce a minimal firewall allowlist text that you can drop into your ticket.

- Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@globex.com>, diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-16 10:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: onboarding evidence & export access patterns

Alex —

Per Diego's note, please find below a concise allowlist and an evidence transfer recipe your infra team can use. I'm keeping it minimal so it can be pasted directly into a firewall ticket.

Minimal firewall allowlist (egress from private deployment):
- Destination: collector.globex-internal.local (customer-hosted)
  Protocol: TCP
  Ports: 443 (TLS/mTLS)
  Notes: Restrict source to the private cluster node subnet; use TLS client cert verification.

- Destination: splunk.collectors.redwood-managed.net
  Protocol: TCP
  Ports: 8088 (HEC), 443 (fallback)
  Notes: If using Redwood forwarder, allowlist Redwood forwarder static egress IPs (see CSV). Prefer mTLS with client cert.

- Destination: s3.amazonaws.com (or your S3 endpoint)
  Protocol: TCP
  Ports: 443
  Notes: For presigned uploads, only outbound HTTPS is required; validate bucket policy.

Evidence handoff recipe (recommended for audits):
1) Trigger export job (on‑demand) that packages logs + manifest and signs the bundle.
2) Upload bundle using presigned PUT to a locked S3 bucket OR push to your Splunk HEC ingestion endpoint with metadata header X-Redwood-Evidence: <sha256>.
3) On receipt, customer infra validates checksums and verifies signed metadata.
4) If requested, Redwoods' runbook will produce a certificate-chain artifact proving mTLS handshake time and cert thumbprints.

Open items for us to confirm with you:
- Do you want automated rotation events included in the evidence bundle (we can include last 30 rotations)?
- Is the preferred transfer pattern presigned S3 or direct HEC ingest?

I'll attach a tiny runbook text file (runbook-obsv-onprem-presigned-urls.txt) with a sample curl command for presigned PUT + a Splunk HEC example. If J. Patel from SecureOps has any specific compliance checks, please loop them in.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Lead Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference

From: J. Patel <jpatel@secureops.co>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Alex Turner <alex.turner@globex.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-09-17 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment observability: onboarding evidence & export access patterns

Kimberly / Diego —

This is excellent and exactly the level of detail we needed for our SOC workstream. Quick answers to your open items: 
- Include the rotation events (last 30) in the evidence bundle — we want provenance for cert rotations.
- Preferred transfer pattern: presigned S3 for audit bundles, Splunk HEC for live telemetry (mTLS).

Two follow-ups from SecureOps: 
1) Can Redwood provide a signed sample bundle with certificate-chain metadata we can validate offline? A small sample (under 5MB) would be ideal for our ingestion test.
2) For the OpenTelemetry traces you mentioned, can you include a small example showing the X-Trace-Id mapping between request logs and span IDs? We need to confirm trace linkage for latency regressions.

If you can send a short sample bundle and a trace-attachment later today or tomorrow we can proceed to schedule the onboarding window. I'll open a ticket (SEC-1849) referencing your HubSpot record.

Regards,
J. Patel
SecureOps — External Audit Lead
